cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Make the Test Test You
cards.instruction: Create a commitment test that gradually exposes what you are unwilling to risk yourself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put your name on the overnight shift. I want to know who is really committed to finishing this project.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will your name be beside mine?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll supervise. Ring me if a decision genuinely needs me; otherwise keep the work moving.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The shift starts at three in the morning. Shall I ring when I arrive?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No, leave me a note for breakfast. I need people who can stay awake without needing me awake beside them.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 sets shift as commitment test; A3 exempts A as supervisor; A5 rules out arrival call and requires breakfast note, exposing protected sleep through authority.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 answers B2 equal signup with remote supervision; A5 uses B4 three-a.m. call offer to delay contact until breakfast.

relationship.evidence: B2 applies test reciprocally and B4 offers a reasonable check-in, forcing the real boundary into view.

heightening.evidence: A5 reveals A unwillingness to be awake in response to B4 specific time, then turns it into another demand on B.

specificity.evidence: A1 project shift and B4 three-a.m. start are enough to grasp the test; breakfast note makes the exemption concrete.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 stay awake without me line exposes hypocrisy without naming a lesson or coaching the reader.
